newsitem.title: USA: New York Life revenue up 10 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: New York Life revenue up 10 percent in 1996.

text.p: New York Life Insurance Co said total revenues, including premiums and investment income, rose 10 percent to $18.3 billion in 1996, but net income fell to $579 million from $625 million in 1995.
Sales of insurance and investment products reached $12.6 billion, spurred by record-setting sales of annuities, guaranteed contracts and mutual funds, New York Life said.
Total premium income from the sale of insurance products rose more than 13 percent to $12.3 billion, it said.
Consolidated assets rose six percent to $78.8 billion during the year, the company said.
Surplus and investment reserves reached $5.6 billion at December 31, 1996, an eight percent jump from 1995.

"In a challenging sales environment, New York Life has registered strong gains in new premiums for insurance, keeping the company among the largest life insurers in terms of market share," New York Life Chief Executive Harry Hohn said.
New York Life said sales of individual annuities rose 27 percent to $1.769 billion in 1996, while new premiums from individual life insurance products topped $683 million.
Sales of variable universal life and variable annuity products rose 85 percent and 145 percent, respectively, with variable annuity sales topping $1 billion for the first time.

New York Life said sales at NYLCare Health Plans Inc, its group health and managed care subsidiary, also posted strong gains. Sales rose 28 percent to $793 million and total revenues exceeded $2.6 billion.
NYLCare was launched in January 1996 when New York Life's group department combined with the company's Sanus Corp Health Systems managed care subsidiary.
New York Life said its assets under management at its asset management business rose 12 percent to over $47 billion in 1996.
Sales from international insurance operations rose more than 13 percent to $66 million.
The company has operations in Argentina, Bermuda, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Mexico, South Korea, Taiwan and the United Kingdom and has representative offices in Shanghai and Guangzhou, China.
